newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO peace negotiators meet in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO peace negotiators meet in West Bank.

text.p: Palestinian and Israeli officials overseeing implementation of PLO-Israel peace deals met on Monday for the first time since Israeli elections last May, witnesses said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat scheduled the talks during their first meeting last week which PLO officials and foreign diplomats said had revived stalled peace talks between the two sides.
The talks took place at the offices of Palestinian chief negotiator Saeb Erekat in the West Bank town of Jericho.

Erekat, head of the Palestinian side in the joint steering and monitoring committee, has said Palestinians would focus talks on Israel's commitment to redeploy its troops in the West Bank town of Hebron.
The Israeli team is headed by former army chief Dan Shomron.
Netanyahu, who has opposed the Hebron troop pullback agreement negotiated by the Labour party government he replaced in June, has rolled the issue to the committee.
The Israeli leader has said he wants to alter the redeployment deal to better safeguard around 400 Jewish settlers living in armed compounds amidst 100,000 Palestinians in the heart of the city.
Palestinians have complained that Netanyahu's government is not honouring its commitments and reject reopening the deal.

Israel evacuated six West Bank cities and nearby villages under interim peace accords with the PLO but delayed its withdrawal from Hebron after Islamic suicide bombings killed 59 people in the Jewish state in February and March.
Palestinians have also called for Israel to implement further troop redeployments in the West Bank which were scheduled to begin on September 7.
